label: thm:ftc2
title: Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement:
Let $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b = [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and have right derivative $f'(x)$ at every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, i.e., $\texttt{HasDerivWithinAt}\; F\; (f'\; x)\; (\mathrm{Ioi}\; x)\; x$ for all such $x$. If $f'$ is interval integrable on $[a,b]$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{IntervalIntegrable}\; f'\; \texttt{volume}\; a\; b$), then
    \[
      \int_a^b f'(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
    In Mathlib this is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}.
proof: Direct application of \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}, given the continuity of $F$ on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b$, the right-derivative hypothesis $\texttt{HasDerivWithinAt}\; F\; (f'\; x)\; (\mathrm{Ioi}\; x)\; x$ for all $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, and $\texttt{IntervalIntegrable}\; f'\; \texttt{volume}\; a\; b$.
